threads.body: [General] `MessagingAttributesExtractor` is also a `SpanKeyProvider`, so this newly assigns `CONSUMER_PROCESS` suppression to the per-message instrumenter even when stable messaging semconv is disabled. With the default semconv suppression strategy, an ambient process span (for example, one from a custom batch instrumenter passed to `TracingSqsMessageHandler`) now suppresses every per-message span; the previous extractor had no span key. To preserve the promised legacy topology, omit the span key in legacy mode and retain it only for the new mode, with a nested-process regression test.

replies.body:
Addressed in 430deafb17dbbc94c3245ba3d46452b8165e1c0f.

Analysis: The migrated per-message extractor exposes the consumer-process span key in every semconv mode, unlike the legacy extractor. Wrapping it only in legacy mode preserves prior span creation while keeping semantic-convention suppression in messaging preview mode. The regression test exercises a custom ambient consumer-process event instrumenter in both modes.

Upsides: Preserves legacy per-message span topology and verifies preview-mode suppression remains enabled.

Downsides: Adds a small mode-dependent wrapper branch and test-only span-key extractor.
